I set myself a challenge to try take a 2d image scene that another artist made and create a 3d animated scene presentation on Sketchfab with it, but only using what was already in the original artwork,  I was given the PSD which made things somewhat easy in terms of layer separation, but I had to paint a lot of extra detail in on certain layers because of the 3d perspective and that the camera would have a few degrees of look around to it.

I struggled with Sketchfab's alpha glitching on this, and it took a while to iron out the layer glitching/ z fighting ,etc, in terms of opacity this is a good example of what Sketchfab can do as there is blending, dithering, additive and refractive opacity all going on at the same time to make this work. Even with the fixes and compromises the alpha still glitches now and again, and there is a loop glitch related to the alpha (I think) that happens when viewing at certain angles.

Naturally I had to take a bunch of liberties with the original art made by Lykke  to create the final piece,  I tried to keep the animation subtle enough as a compliment to presenting a "still image" , so the animated effects are kept subtle / atmospheric / environmental only, and these effects include.

- Water volume, slowly flowing 
- Refractive wavy effect under water as the water flows
- Subtle particulates appear/disappear in water (glinting effect)
- Background mist gently blowing to the left, this layer also implies spray coming from the water fall on the right
- Foreground mist/fog layer,  similar to the background fog but different texture/hue,   both layers combined help to imply volumetrics
- Pollen/gust particulates appear/disappear in air (glinting effect)

I wasn't sure how the heck I was going to approach doing the waterfalls, actually wasn't intending to animate them at all, but I got the idea to steal one of the animated mist elements and move scale/rotate move it in from of one of the water falls, changed the material to refractive bump scrolling , fiddled with uv on Sketchfab and eventually I got a reasonable water fall effect.

Nothing here is perfect anyway but I am fairly happy with the result and once again impressed how far Sketchfab can go.
